content:
Just to be clear, you don't have a "Thunderbird account." Thunderbird is a program that you can use to manage accounts at external email providers such as Gmail, Yahoo, AOL, Comcast, etc.

So. assuming your email is with those or the like, all you need is an Internet connection. It shouldn't matter to Thunderbird or the email provider how you get there, just that you can get there.

Consider that I have a Gmail account, and I have Thunderbird installed on my laptop. I can travel anywhere where I can connect to the Internet, be it a hotel, airport, library, etc. and I can send and receive my email without changing anything.

content:
A couple of things...

- Cookies must be enabled in Thunderbird for OAuth2 authorization to work. See <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Accept cookies from sites>. It might also help to remove any existing cookies for that account from <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Show Cookies>. And remove any existing OAuth tokens for Gmail found in <Settings | Privacy & Security | Saved Passwords>. Then restart Thunderbird and try again.

- Anti-virus programs are notorious for interfering with email traffic. Bitdefender is often cited. Try temporarily disabling it or creating an exception in it to stop scanning email.
